### STATISTICIAN | ACTUARY | DATA SCIENTIST

I work across health metrics, actuarial modelling, machine learning, and data visualisation. My focus is on making analytical work clear, practical, and reproducible, using R and Python.

My background spans insurance and pensions, research, and teaching. Following the COVID-19 outbreak, I began focusing on health data and infectious disease modelling. As a member of the Global Burden of Disease collaborator network, I contribute to the review of global health research.

I am the author of *Health Metrics and the Spread of Infectious Diseases: Machine Learning Applications and Spatial Modelling Analysis with R*, published by CRC Press in 2025. The book brings together health metrics, statistical methods, and worked examples in R. [Explore the book and its companion resources](/content/books/posts/hmsid/index.qmd).

As a certified Carpentries instructor, I teach programming, data wrangling, statistical modelling, and reproducible workflows. My [workshops and recorded materials](/about/workshops/index.qmd) support learners in moving from concepts to practical analysis.

I lead R-Ladies Rome and Rome R Users Group, organising events where people can learn, share their work, and build connections. I also develop [R packages](/content/rpackages/index.qmd) and share examples through my writing and open-source projects.

My current work connects research, teaching, and [DataMetricus consultancy](/consultancy.qmd). In [Notes on Data and Learning](/content/newsletter/index.qmd), I reflect on data, modelling, and what we learn through practice.
